text: `Lets say the refreshrate is 24 hertz, and the current video playing is 23.976 fps, then you want to speed up the clock by 0.1% to make the vblank ticks increment the same as the video timestamps, but if the video is 23.976 fps but is reported as 24 fps th"
body:
`Lets say the refreshrate is 24 hertz, and the current video playing is 23.976 fps, then you want to speed up the clock by 0.1% to make the vblank ticks increment the same as the video timestamps, but if the video is 23.976 fps but is reported as 24 fps this won't happen.`

I need to take another look I guess. If refresh rate is 24Hz (or 23.976Hz) and stream hint is 23.976 then you get a speed factor of 1.001, and unfactored clock interval of 1/24, so with speed factor applied 1/23.976 tick intervals so clock is effectively sped up (from the rounded approximate version) - agreed.  If hint is incorrect then CalcFrameRate() spots that and fixes m_fFrameRate and reconfigures renderer right? Does this not end up being catered for in clock?  That I need to check.  But that is the correct place to fix it if not already the case.  Drifting the clock along with any pts drift gives a moving target for any other sync operations - so I agree when bad streams are detected the clock tick should adjust but it should be a clear decision and clear event to change.

`CDVDClock::GetClock() is a clock based on g_VideoReferenceClock with an offset, CDVDClock::GetClock() basically returns the current playback position, the perfect time to present a frame is when the value from CDVDClock::GetClock() is the same as the pts (you can probably never get this close but this is the idea).` Agreed except that that as I stated earlier the display pts should match the GetClock() value - and that is most certainly NOT the present value.

`The rendermanager uses CDVDClock::GetAbsoluteClock() for timing, when dvdplayer pushes out a frame it has to convert the pts from a value from CDVDClock::GetClock() into a value from CDVDClock::GetAbsoluteClock().`  Actually rendermanager really uses WaitAbsoluteClock() but I know what you mean.

`Since CDVDClock::GetAbsoluteClock() is also clock derived from g_VideoReferenceClock and also with an offset, all you have to do to convert a pts into a presenttime is add the offset between g_VideoReferenceClock and CDVDClock::GetClock() and subtract the offset between g_VideoReferenceClock and CDVDClock::GetAbsoluteClock().`  I know they are offsets but currently rendermanager does not do that - it knows nothing about GetClock -> g_VideoReferenceClock conversion - you are suggesting introducing that which is not a problem- but was not clear from how you described.  More importantly though you are moving the timing of the sleep calculation until you get to the Wait condition - which is the crux of it (ie avoids the need for any of the sleep calculations in OutputPicture - which I for one would be happy to see the back of because currently it is a mess).  You are basically going in the direction I alluded to.  Give rendermanager the pts and playspeed and let it work out the correct sleep/wait time, and add a rendermanager function for DVDPlayerVideo to query the current display pts (and interpolated pts too).  This is precisely what I am working on right now with FernetMenta.

`Regarding the rest of your code changes though, I'm the one who has to support this part of XBMC for years to come, I never commit anything until I have a very good understanding of what I'm doing, and I can prove to myself that what I have done works correct.`

I would not expect anything less and just hope that some of my ideas or not quickly dismissed due to my inability to explain them - because believe it or not I feel I have thoroughly analysed this part of xbmc.

body:
The first thing is if you URLDecode you need only URLDecode the filename,
not the entire thing, right?  After all, the rest of the path comes from a
filesystem that is NOT to be URLDecode'd.

The second is whether it should be done at all.  As elupus points out, you
miss the case where the file is 01%20-%20track.mp3 and it's NOT url encoded.

It would be better to decode only if it makes sense to do so - some sort of
"copying from a source that's always URL encoded to a source that is never
url encoded" would be the only case you need do anything.

text: That would be nice, but more complex. We can't detect mid-stream sample rate changes without calling the decoder (unless the container informs us of that, which e.g. mpegts doesn't do), which we currently don't do at all when passthrough in use. And if t"
body:
That would be nice, but more complex.
We can't detect mid-stream sample rate changes without calling the decoder (unless the container informs us of that, which e.g. mpegts doesn't do), which we currently don't do at all when passthrough in use.
And if the sample rate changes to a passthrough-compatible one, we don't (with the current code) want to start passthrough as the chances of it switching back to an incompatible one are high and we wouldn't detect it anymore.

However, AudioEngine can detect sample rate changes during passthrough, so this can be revisited then :)
